correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite nonnegative h with h(0)>0, reconstructing the parking protocol gives W_h(sigma)=product F(ell_i). Splitting at sigma_k=n factors weights into left/right standardized permutations; inversion parity separates as (-1)^(n-k) times a q=-1 subset sum. The exact coefficient product evaluates to G(n-1,k-1), causing cancellation for n odd and k even. Every denominator is positive due to the zero-displacement outcome. The provided checker independently enumerates preference vectors and outcomes for five weights and 855 exact assertions; no infinite claim rests on experiments.

originality.rationale: The original contribution is restricted to a universal explicit conditional K-position sign law, especially exact even/odd balance when n is odd and K even for any nonnegative displacement kernel; the uniform and unit-interval full-outcome enumerators and unconditional signed statistics are recognized as existing. Pinsky 2024 and Celano et al. 2025/2026 are materially inspected strong comparators. The Gaussian-binomial cross-label cancellation is not displayed in their compared claims. This is best-knowledge originality, not historical certification.
residual_risks: Theorem 4.3 of arxiv:2507.07243v2 is a general weighted outcome statistic generating formula which implicitly determines the conditional parity for its restricted kernels; the nontrivial explicit conditional evaluation and arbitrary h universality are the only novelty asserted.
An earlier unpublished or unindexed analysis could have performed the same maximum-label Gaussian-binomial conditioning; historical uniqueness is not established.
The lucky-car paper arxiv:2410.08057 was assessed at abstract level only; direct overlap appears less likely but not excluded.

value.rationale: The joint parity and final-car location law is a canonical conditional statistic in random linear probing. The precise positional fairness is invariant under all nonnegative per-car displacement penalties and all odd orders, which is a structural theorem beyond the known unconditional counts. The general all-k formula and finite recurrences explain the nonzero cases and make the phenomenon operationally testable. The full prior generating-function results are acknowledged, so the mathematical value rests on the nontrivial evaluated conditional refinement.
